title: A Warm Nose at the Door: The Everyday Magic of Pet Companionship
title_zh: 门口的温暖鼻尖：宠物陪伴的日常魔法
intro_zh: 本文约900词，含6个核心词，难度适中，适合CET-4水平。

paragraphs.en: Every evening when I open the door, my dog Bella is already there, tail wagging, eyes bright. She doesn’t ask about my day or give advice. She simply presses her warm nose into my hand and follows me into the kitchen. In that moment, the stress of work seems to shrink. This feeling is not just in my head. Scientists have found that living with a pet can bring real emotional and physical benefits, and the companionship of an animal is more powerful than many of us realize.
paragraphs.zh: 每天傍晚一打开门，我的狗贝拉已经在那里，摇晃着尾巴，眼睛明亮。她不会问我今天过得怎么样，也不会给建议。她只是把温暖的鼻子贴到我的手上，然后跟着我走进厨房。那一刻，工作的压力似乎缩小了。这种感觉不只是我的想象。科学家发现，与宠物一起生活能带来真实的情感和身体益处，而动物的陪伴比我们许多人意识到的更强大。

paragraphs.en: Dogs and cats are surprisingly good at reading human emotions. Research shows that dogs can perceive changes in our facial expressions and even our smell when we are happy or stressed. In one study, dogs were shown pictures of happy and angry faces. They responded differently, and their heart rates changed. When we are sad, a pet may lie quietly beside us or lick our hands. This gentle action can soothe us in ways that words cannot.
paragraphs.zh: 狗和猫出乎意料地擅长解读人类情绪。研究表明，当我们开心或紧张时，狗能感知我们面部表情的变化，甚至我们的气味。在一项研究中，狗被展示开心和愤怒的脸的图片。它们反应不同，心率也会改变。当我们难过时，宠物可能会静静地躺在旁边，或舔舔我们的手。这种温柔的动作能以言语无法做到的方式安慰我们。

paragraphs.en: The emotional benefits of pets are especially clear for people who live alone. Many people feel a deep sense of anxiety and loneliness in big cities. A pet provides a constant presence. Feeding, walking, and talking to an animal gives structure to the day and reduces the feeling of being disconnected from the world. A 2018 survey in the United States found that 74 percent of pet owners said their mental health improved because of their pets. The simple act of stroking a cat or dog can lower stress hormones and increase feelings of calm.
paragraphs.zh: 宠物带来的情感益处对于独居者尤其明显。许多人在大城市里感到深深的焦虑和孤独。宠物提供了一个持续的存在。喂养、遛狗和与动物说话给日常生活带来了节奏，减少了与世界脱节的感觉。2018年美国一项调查发现，74%的宠物主人表示他们的心理健康因为宠物而改善。仅仅抚摸猫或狗这种简单的动作就能降低压力荷尔蒙，增加平静感。

paragraphs.en: Pets also help us connect with other people. Walking a dog naturally invites conversation. Neighbors stop to ask the dog’s name and age. In parks, dog owners often become friends. This social effect is not limited to dog walkers. People who keep cats or birds often share photos and stories online, building communities. In a world where many young adults feel isolated, pets act as a social bridge. They give us an easy, natural reason to talk to strangers — a small but meaningful step toward friendship.
paragraphs.zh: 宠物还帮助我们与他人建立联系。遛狗自然而然地引发交谈。邻居们会停下来问狗的名字和年龄。在公园里，狗主人常常成为朋友。这种社交效应不仅限于遛狗者。养猫或养鸟的人经常在网上分享照片和故事，建立社区。在一个许多年轻人感到孤立的世界里，宠物充当了社交桥梁。它们给了我们一个轻松自然地和陌生人交谈的理由——这是走向友谊的小而有意义的一步。

paragraphs.en: The physical benefits are just as remarkable. People with pets often have lower blood pressure and a slower resting heart rate. Dogs need daily exercise, which means their owners get more physical activity. A study from the American Heart Association reported that dog owners are 24 percent less likely to die from heart disease compared with non-owners. Even simply keeping a fish tank can reduce stress in a waiting room. These findings suggest that caring for a living being encourages us to take better care of ourselves.
paragraphs.zh: 身体方面的益处同样显著。养宠物的人通常血压更低，静息心率更慢。狗需要日常运动，这意味着主人能得到更多身体活动。美国心脏协会的一项研究报告称，与不养狗的人相比，养狗者死于心脏病的可能性低24%。甚至只是养一缸鱼也能减少候诊室里的压力。这些发现表明，照顾一个生命会鼓励我们更好地照顾自己。

paragraphs.en: One of the most precious gifts pets offer is their unconditional love. They do not care if we fail an exam, lose a job, or feel socially awkward. Their affection does not depend on our success. This kind of acceptance is rare in human relationships. Psychologists say that such consistent, non-judgmental support builds self-esteem and resilience. Knowing that a cat curls up on our lap no matter what happens gives us a safe emotional base. It reminds us that we are worthy of love simply for being ourselves.
paragraphs.zh: 宠物给我们的最珍贵礼物之一就是它们无条件的爱。它们不在乎我们考试是否失败、是否失业或是否在社交中表现得笨拙。它们的喜爱不取决于我们的成功。这种接纳在人际关系中很少见。心理学家说，这种持续的、不带评判的支持能建立自尊和韧性。知道无论发生什么，一只猫都会蜷缩在我们的膝上，给了我们一个安全的情感基地。它提醒我们，仅仅因为做自己，我们就值得被爱。

paragraphs.en: For children, growing up with a pet can be a powerful lesson in responsibility and empathy. When a child helps feed or walk a family dog, they learn that another being depends on them. They begin to recognize the needs and feelings of others. Studies have shown that children with pets tend to have higher emotional intelligence and show more caring behavior toward classmates. A pet can also be a trusted companion during difficult teenage years, providing a non-judgmental ear when friends are not available.
paragraphs.zh: 对于孩子来说，与宠物一起成长可以成为责任感和同理心的有力一课。当孩子帮忙喂养或遛家里的狗时，他们懂得另一个生命依赖他们。他们开始认识到他人的需求和感受。研究表明，养宠物的孩子往往有更高的情商，并对同学表现出更多的关心行为。在困难的青少年时期，宠物也可以成为值得信赖的伙伴，在没有朋友倾听时提供不带评判的耳朵。

paragraphs.en: Older adults often face loneliness after retirement or the loss of a spouse. Pets give them a reason to get up in the morning. A senior with a small dog must go outside several times a day, which encourages light exercise and contact with neighbors. Some care homes have even adopted resident cats, and nurses report that residents are more talkative and less depressed. The companionship of an animal can fill the silence with gentle routine and purpose. It is not a cure for grief, but it is a daily comfort that says: you are still needed.
paragraphs.zh: 老年人经常在退休或失去配偶后面临孤独。宠物给了他们早起的理由。养一只小狗的老年人必须每天外出几次，这促进了轻度运动和与邻居的接触。一些养老院甚至收养了常驻猫，护士报告说居民更爱说话，抑郁也更少。动物的陪伴能以温和的日常和目的感填补寂静。它不是悲伤的治愈，但它是一份日常安慰，告诉我们：你仍然被需要。

paragraphs.en: In the end, the bond between humans and animals is a two-way street. We provide food, shelter, and medical care; they give us loyalty, joy, and meaning. But this gift comes with responsibility. A pet is not a toy — it is a living being that depends on us for life. When we make the choice to welcome an animal into our home, we open our heart to a relationship that can transform ordinary days into something special. The warm nose at the door is not just a greeting. It is a reminder that love, in its simplest form, is always there for us.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，人与动物之间的纽带是双向的。我们提供食物、住所和医疗；它们给我们忠诚、快乐和意义。但这份礼物伴随着责任。宠物不是玩具——它是一个依赖我们生存的生命。当我们选择欢迎一只动物进入我们的家时，我们敞开心扉，迎接一种能让平凡日子变得特别的关系。门口的温暖鼻尖不仅仅是问候。它提醒我们，爱，以最简单的形式，始终为我们而在。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Pets can help people live longer.
Pets provide emotional and practical support to humans.
People who own pets are better citizens.
questions.explain: 主旨题。文章从多个方面（情感、社交、身体、儿童、老人）阐述了宠物给人类带来的益处，因此B项'宠物为人类提供情感和实际支持'最为全面。A项只是身体益处的一部分，不全面；C项无根据；D项没有提到。

questions.q: According to paragraph 3, what percentage of pet owners in the 2018 survey said their mental health improved because of their pets?
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段明确提到'74 percent of pet owners said their mental health improved'，因此选C（下标2）。A是心脏病的比例，B和D未提及。

questions.q: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about pets?
options: Pets are helpful for social communication.
questions.explain: 推断题。第四段指出遛狗促进交谈，养猫养鸟的人也在网上建立社区，因此可推断宠物有助于社交。B项'always'过于绝对；C项与原文相反；D项'Only'过于绝对，原文提到多种宠物。

questions.q: In the sentence 'Psychologists say that such consistent, non-judgmental support builds self-esteem and resilience,' the word 'resilience' most likely means?
options: the ability to recover quickly from difficulties
questions.explain: 词义题。根据语境，'resilience'与自尊心并列，且是'非评判性支持'带来的积极结果，结合常识可推断为'从困难中快速恢复的能力'，故选A。
